title: Stage 8: Shipping it
summary: The boss stage: fail gracefully, report statistics, group the routes and finish the service.

steps.title: Final stage: ship it
body: Your API reads, creates, updates, deletes, filters, pages, stores its data behind an interface and guards it with a key. Three jobs stand between it and something you could put in front of real clients:
1. **Fail gracefully.** When your code throws, the client should get a tidy `500` with a JSON body, and never a stack trace.
2. **Report on itself.** A `/stats` endpoint that summarises the tasks.
3. **Tidy up and add one more feature.** Group the `/tasks` routes, then add an endpoint that completes every task at once.
This is the boss stage: there are no new teaching cards between the steps. Each prompt is a spec with everything you need.

steps.title: Fail gracefully
prompt: Sooner or later some handler will throw: a bug, a null, a database that is down. Today that gives the caller a bare `500` with no body. With the wrong settings it could give them a full stack trace, which tells an attacker a lot about your code.
**1. Add an endpoint that fails on purpose**, so there is something to test against. It is public, like `/health`:
**2. Add an error-handling middleware.** It wraps the rest of the pipeline in `try` / `catch`:
- An exception thrown anywhere later in the pipeline becomes `500 Internal Server Error` with a JSON body `{"error":"..."}`.

- The message is general. It must not contain the exception's message (`Boom`), its type name, or a stack trace. Those details are for you, not for the caller: write them to the log with `app.Logger.LogError(ex, "Unhandled exception");`.
- The server keeps running and answers the next request normally.
- Requests that do not throw are untouched. A `404` stays a `404`.
- The `500` response still carries `X-Request-Id`. That id is what a user can quote to you when they report the failure.
Add this middleware **first**, before the other two. The outermost layer of the pipeline is the only place from which it can catch what every later layer throws.
Everything else must keep working, including the API key.

static string Ids(JsonElement json) => json.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Array
? string.Join(",", json.EnumerateArray().Select(e => DojoWeb.Prop(e, "id")))
: "(not a JSON array)";
static JsonElement At(JsonElement json, int index) =>
json.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Array && index < json.GetArrayLength() ? json[index] : default;
static async Task<string> IdsOf(HttpClient http, string url) => Ids(await DojoWeb.Json(await http.GetAsync(url)));
static bool HasError(JsonElement json) => !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(DojoWeb.Prop(json, "error"));
static Task<HttpResponseMessage> Patch(HttpClient http, string url, object body) =>
http.PatchAsync(url, JsonContent.Create(body));
static string? RequestId(HttpResponseMessage response) =>
response.Headers.TryGetValues("X-Request-Id", out var values) ? string.Join(",", values) : null;
static void HasRequestId(string what, HttpResponseMessage response) =>
Dojo.Check(what + " has an X-Request-Id header", !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(RequestId(response)), "the header was missing or empty");
static void Percent(string name, double expected, JsonElement stats)
var raw = DojoWeb.Prop(stats, "percentDone");
var ok = double.TryParse(raw, System.Globalization.NumberStyles.Float, System.Globalization.CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, out var actual)
&& Math.Abs(actual - expected) < 0.0001;

static async Task Stats(HttpClient http, string when, int total, int done, int open, double percent)
var stats = await DojoWeb.Json(await http.GetAsync("/stats"));
Dojo.Eq(when + ", total is " + total, total.ToString(), DojoWeb.Prop(stats, "total"));
Dojo.Eq(when + ", done is " + done, done.ToString(), DojoWeb.Prop(stats, "done"));
Dojo.Eq(when + ", open is " + open, open.ToString(), DojoWeb.Prop(stats, "open"));
Percent(when + ", percentDone is " + percent.ToString(System.Globalization.CultureInfo.InvariantCulture), percent, stats);

prompt: Add `GET /stats`, a summary of all tasks. It is public: no API key, like `/health`.
| `percentDone` | `done` as a percentage of `total`, a number rounded to one decimal place: 1 of 3 is `33.3`, 2 of 3 is `66.7`, 2 of 4 is `50` |

- Watch the arithmetic: `1 / 3` with two `int`s is `0`.

steps.title: Group the routes, complete them all
prompt: Six endpoints repeat the prefix `/tasks`. A **route group** states it once:

Each route in the group is the group's prefix plus its own pattern. Move all the `/tasks` endpoints into a group made with `app.MapGroup("/tasks")`. Their behaviour must not change at all. One thing to watch: the `Location` header of a created task is still the full path, `/tasks/4`.
Add `POST /tasks/complete-all`, which marks every task as done.
- `updated` is the number of tasks that changed, meaning those that were not done before. Calling it again straight away gives `{"updated":0}`.
- Titles and ids do not change.
- It lives under `/tasks`, so it needs the API key like the rest: `401` without it.

- A good home for the work is a new method on `ITaskStore`, for example `int CompleteAll();`, so that it happens inside the store's lock. Looping over `GetAll()` and calling `Update` from the endpoint works too.

// "1,2,3" for a JSON array of tasks, so one row can check which tasks came back and in what order.
static string Ids(JsonElement json) => json.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Array
? string.Join(",", json.EnumerateArray().Select(e => DojoWeb.Prop(e, "id")))
: "(not a JSON array)";
static JsonElement At(JsonElement json, int index) =>
json.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Array && index < json.GetArrayLength() ? json[index] : default;
static async Task<string> IdsOf(HttpClient http, string url) => Ids(await DojoWeb.Json(await http.GetAsync(url)));
static bool HasError(JsonElement json) => !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(DojoWeb.Prop(json, "error"));
static Task<HttpResponseMessage> Patch(HttpClient http, string url, object body) =>
http.PatchAsync(url, JsonContent.Create(body));
static string? RequestId(HttpResponseMessage response) =>
response.Headers.TryGetValues("X-Request-Id", out var values) ? string.Join(",", values) : null;
static void HasRequestId(string what, HttpResponseMessage response) =>
Dojo.Check(what + " has an X-Request-Id header", !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(RequestId(response)), "the header was missing or empty");
static void Percent(string name, double expected, JsonElement stats)
var raw = DojoWeb.Prop(stats, "percentDone");
var ok = double.TryParse(raw, System.Globalization.NumberStyles.Float, System.Globalization.CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, out var actual)
&& Math.Abs(actual - expected) < 0.0001;
Dojo.Check(name, ok, "percentDone was " + (raw ?? "missing"));
static async Task Stats(HttpClient http, string when, int total, int done, int open, double percent)
var stats = await DojoWeb.Json(await http.GetAsync("/stats"));
Dojo.Eq(when + ", total is " + total, total.ToString(), DojoWeb.Prop(stats, "total"));
Dojo.Eq(when + ", done is " + done, done.ToString(), DojoWeb.Prop(stats, "done"));
Dojo.Eq(when + ", open is " + open, open.ToString(), DojoWeb.Prop(stats, "open"));
Percent(when + ", percentDone is " + percent.ToString(System.Globalization.CultureInfo.InvariantCulture), percent, stats);

steps.title: What you built
body: Read your `Program.cs` once more from the top. It is a complete small web service:
- **Resources and methods**: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` on `/tasks`, each with the semantics HTTP promises (safe reads, idempotent replaces and deletes).
- **Honest status codes**: `200`, `201` with `Location`, `204`, `400`, `401`, `404`, and a controlled `500`.
- **Validation** with one error shape, `{"error":"..."}`, everywhere.
- **Filtering, searching and paging** from the query string, with limits the client cannot talk its way past.
- **Dependency injection**: storage behind `ITaskStore`, registered once, injected where needed, and safe under concurrent requests.
- **Middleware**: error handling, request ids and an API key, each written once for the whole API.
These ideas carry over to every web framework you will meet. The method names change. HTTP stays the same.
## What a production API adds next
None of these are built here, but you now know where each one plugs in:
| Next step | What it replaces or adds |
| **A database with EF Core** | A new `ITaskStore` implementation, registered as *scoped*. No endpoint changes, which is the payoff of stage 6. |
| **OpenAPI / Swagger** | A machine-readable description of your endpoints, and a web page for trying them out. |
| **Real authentication** | Users and tokens (JWT, OAuth) through the built-in authentication and authorization middleware, in place of one shared key. |
| **Structured logging** | `ILogger` everywhere, with the request id attached to every line. |
| **`ProblemDetails`** | The standard JSON shape for errors, and `app.UseExceptionHandler()` in place of your hand-written `try` / `catch`. |
| **Automated tests** | `WebApplicationFactory` starts your API in memory and calls it over HTTP, which is very close to what the dojo's tests have been doing all along. |
